question: Does the Earth go round the Sun?

The Earth takes approximately 365.24 days to complete one orbit around the Sun. This is why we have a leap year every four years, to account for the extra fraction of a day.

The reason the Earth orbits the Sun is due to the gravitational pull between the two bodies. The Sun's massive size and gravity cause the Earth to follow an elliptical path around it.

This concept is often referred to as the heliocentric model, which was first proposed by Nicolaus Copernicus in the 16th century and later supported by scientists like Galileo Galilei and Johannes Kepler. Today, it's widely accepted as the accurate description of our solar system.
